broeringluke: Roland "Doc" Broeringluke arrived on Day 5 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.

The barrage caught Roland "Doc" Broeringluke in the open at S-S10. The medic tied two tourniquets and shouted for a bed. The shell that hit S-S10 took Roland "Doc" Broeringluke with it. No stretcher, no surgeon, no last words. Just the crater.

Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke put a cracked shaving mirror beside the bunk. Someone who had known Roland "Doc" Broeringluke helped clear the shelf without saying why. Day 6. The Hegemony took Hill 304. From the heights Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
The section held a competition for the worst joke. Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke won before reaching the end of his entry.
Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke passed ration containers down a chain of hands. By the time supper reached the front, every man smelled of it.
Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke brushed dried mud off a letter and found one more word under it: 'soon'. He wished the rest of the sentence had survived.
The new recruit kept closing both eyes to aim. Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke spent the afternoon helping until one eye stayed open.

A periscope poked up from the enemy line. Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke shot it to pieces, and the man holding it, Quentin Stefan, was grazed. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal, and the orders at S-S10 changed before the cheering ended. Quentin "Parson" Broeringluke shouldered another load.
bucket_hat_pat_: The new rifleman is Jonas Pat, once a lamplighter from Ashford Vale. The corporal asked if a lamplighter was any use in a trench. Jonas Pat said he would find out.
Day 10: Blackwater Canal was lost. Jonas Pat wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
davebowlton: Walter Davebowlton came up on Day 9 carrying news from Ashford Vale. A man interrupted to ask whether the railway clock had been repaired.

Walter Davebowlton went over the top with the night raiders, face black with soot. In the Concord trench a man turned around too late. Gideon "Ghost" Marks did not get up again. (@marks89kk) Walter Davebowlton went over with the raiders and dropped into the Concord trench. Yann Vylet was hit hard before the whistle called everyone back. (@simon_vylet) Walter Davebowlton walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
frank_mart00: At the depot, Matthias Mart had practised answering to his name. At R-F7, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.

A child had enclosed a riddle in a parcel for Matthias Mart. The answer was on the back. He kept the dugout guessing until supper. Verdel Ridge has been won. Matthias Mart listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
The company barber offered a choice of haircuts. Matthias Mart asked to see the second one. The barber laughed.

On a quiet night Matthias Mart (Concord) and Ulrich Jwessels (Hegemony) called out their names across no man's land, just to hear another voice. Now each knows exactly who is out there. A letter from home found Matthias Mart before the night shift. Matthias Mart folded it small and kept it close.

Matthias Mart went out with the wiring party at R-F7. Crawl, hammer a stake, pull the wire, crawl back. Nobody was hit. Hill 304 is in Hegemony hands. Matthias Mart stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
Matthias Mart traded a tin whistle for two cigarettes and immediately regretted it.
Dawn watch. Matthias Mart put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Casimir Sky, badly wounded.
Matthias Mart found a photograph in the mud of no man's land: a woman in a white dress, and a name on the back that is not from his side of the wire.
Matthias Mart measured the remaining pencil against the remaining paper. For once, the supplies seemed likely to run out together.

At R-F7 a shape dropped into the trench out of the night. Matthias Mart turned around and took a shovel blow. Konrad Dorf of the Hegemony was already gone. Raider: Konrad Dorf of the Hegemony (@hunter_dorf0629). The Hegemony hold Blackwater Canal now, and they can see straight into R-F7. Matthias Mart has learned to walk bent double.
lancegribko: The old hands of R-F22 have been here since Day 1. Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko has been here since Day 4. In a trench, that difference already feels like years.
A parcel arrived tied with blue ribbon. Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko gave the contents away and kept the ribbon to mark a page.

Wiring party. Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko held the coil while two others pulled. Twenty yards of new wire at R-F22, and everyone came back. Day 6. The Hegemony took Hill 304. From the heights Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.

Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko tried to remember the sound of the church bell in Kesselby. Every version sounded like the ration bell. Mail came up the line with a letter for Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko. Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
The shelling stopped while Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko was counting the seconds between hits. He kept counting anyway, and waited a long time before moving.
Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko and Benedikt "Mole" Twenskyyy compared drawings of home. Both drawings included a kitchen table larger than the house.

A bullet hit Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko's belt buckle at R-F22 and glanced off into his side. Shallow, the medic said. He is keeping the buckle. Shot by Arno Coopergfulto of the Concord (@coopergfulton).

Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko returned to R-F22 with a fresh bandage and orders to keep it dry. He has already broken the second part. The Hegemony secured Blackwater Canal. Clement "Hollow" Lancegribko helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.
owenhart247: Felix "Bones" Owenhart reached S-F13 expecting a speech. The welcome consisted of a mug, a space on a bench and directions to the latrine.
Felix "Bones" Owenhart was in the first hundred. The old hands in S-F13 call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.
Felix "Bones" Owenhart sharpened a pencil with great care and then could not think what to write. He put the date at the top anyway.
Verdel Ridge fell to the Concord at dusk. Felix "Bones" Owenhart helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
Felix "Bones" Owenhart fired at a movement across the wire at S-F13. The man went down: Florian "Shadow" Slightlyreta, badly wounded.

Felix "Bones" Owenhart was hit through the chest at S-F13. He is breathing. That is all the medic would say. Shot by Severin Heheheha of the Hegemony (@heheheha1939). A rifle cracked from the far side of no man's land. Felix "Bones" Owenhart fell at S-F13 and never moved again. Shot by Severin Heheheha of the Hegemony (@heheheha1939).

The papers connected Edmund Owenhart to Felix "Bones" Owenhart. The men took longer to learn Edmund Owenhart's own habits, but they made the effort. Volunteer number 75. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on Edmund Owenhart's tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.'

A clear shot from S-F13. Edmund Owenhart gravely wounded Dorian Coletonmarti and slid back down below the parapet. After the loss of Hill 304, Edmund Owenhart helped stack spare sandbags at S-F13. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
Edmund Owenhart spent the evening teaching a recruit to sew. The recruit pricked a finger and accused the needle of taking sides.
Edmund Owenhart found an old shopping list inside a coat pocket. Soap, lamp oil, apples. He folded it along the original creases.
Edmund Owenhart fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Gustav Coletonmarti, gravely wounded. Nobody nearby said anything.

A round came through the loophole Edmund Owenhart was watching at S-F13 and hit him in the collarbone. He is alive and very angry. Shot by Norbert Fransinlak of the Hegemony (@fransinlak). Edmund Owenhart borrowed the sergeant's periscope, found a target, handed it back, and fired. Nils Axebozo was grazed. Edmund Owenhart was killed at S-F13 just after dawn. The cup of tea beside him was still hot. Shot by Norbert Fransinlak of the Hegemony (@fransinlak).

Zeno Owenhart asked about Edmund Owenhart on arriving at S-F13. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another. Zeno Owenhart was among the first hundred through the depot gates. The First Wave ribbon is the only clean thing he owns.

Zeno Owenhart went over with the raiders and dropped into the Hegemony trench. Quentin "Spark" Josiascouper was hit hard before the whistle called everyone back. (@josiascouper) Zeno Owenhart jumped into the Hegemony trench and swung the shovel at the first shape that moved. It was Ulrich Zelenszki. The Hegemony medics will be busy. (@_zelenszki_) Zeno Owenhart came back from the night raid on two stretcher poles. Nobody is sure which side fired the shot. The Hegemony hold Blackwater Canal now, and they can see straight into S-F13. Zeno Owenhart has learned to walk bent double.
pridumay_sam_mne_vpadlu: The draft reached Q-F14 on Day 9. Ulrich "Owl" Vpadlu was shown which board tipped, which roof leaked and which promises to ignore.

Ulrich "Owl" Vpadlu was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at Q-F14. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Dorian Itzwill of the Concord (@itzwill16). Ulrich "Owl" Vpadlu walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
sanocfc: The new rifleman is Norbert Sanocfc, once a tailor from Halden. The corporal asked if a tailor was any use in a trench. Norbert Sanocfc said he would find out.

No rifles, only shovels and knives. Norbert Sanocfc dropped into the Concord trench by a dugout door and met Karel Punchworth coming out. It was over in seconds. (@lord_punchworth) Blackwater Canal has been won. Norbert Sanocfc listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.
schradog2: Casimir Schradog arrived with the Day 3 draft, carrying his mother's thimble and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Casimir Schradog stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
Casimir Schradog polished a spoon until he could see a small, bent version of his face. It looked unimpressed with supper too.

Casimir Schradog borrowed a magnifying glass to read cramped handwriting. The urgently needed word turned out to be 'cabbage'. A letter from home reached Casimir Schradog before dusk. Casimir Schradog read it twice and slept a little easier.

Casimir Schradog went out with the wiring party at S-F6. Crawl, hammer a stake, pull the wire, crawl back. Nobody was hit. A letter from home reached Casimir Schradog before dusk. Casimir Schradog read it twice and slept a little easier. The Hegemony flag went up over Hill 304. Casimir Schradog did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.

Casimir Schradog agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made him look twice his age. A letter from home reached Casimir Schradog before dusk. Casimir Schradog read it twice and slept a little easier.

Casimir Schradog fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Otto Commanderchr, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything. A letter from home reached Casimir Schradog before dusk. Casimir Schradog read it twice and slept a little easier.

A tin cup glinted on the enemy parapet. Casimir Schradog aimed just below it. Otto "Saint" Kamdensipple was grazed. A letter from home reached Casimir Schradog before dusk. Casimir Schradog read it twice and slept a little easier.

The artist tried again while Casimir Schradog read a letter. The new portrait was better, though the ears became the subject of discussion. A letter from home reached Casimir Schradog before dusk. Casimir Schradog read it twice and slept a little easier.

Casimir Schradog came back from the raid with mud to the eyebrows and an enemy helmet as a souvenir. Nobody heard the Concord raiders cut the wire. Casimir Schradog only heard boots on the duckboards at S-F6, then nothing but pain. Raider: Albin Belugawales of the Concord (@belugawales3). The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Blackwater Canal. Casimir Schradog folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside. A letter from home reached Casimir Schradog before dusk. Casimir Schradog read it twice and slept a little easier.
scrawny_ronnnie: Emil "Shadow" Ronnnie stepped off the supply cart at R-S1 and stood very still, listening to the guns as if they were saying his name.
Emil "Shadow" Ronnnie walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.

Bram Wade walked the captured trenches of Blackwater Canal and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir. A letter from home reached Bram Wade before dusk. Bram Wade read it twice and slept a little easier.
wellington21324: Day 8. The corporal put Dorian Wellington beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.
Dorian Wellington offered to read the newspaper aloud. The audience asked for the advertisements first, then the racing results, and the war last.
The Hegemony hold Blackwater Canal now, and they can see straight into S-S2. Dorian Wellington has learned to walk bent double.
